record.context_brief: Counterexamples via weak limits of perturbed solutions
record.original_question: For the p = n harmonic-map system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = |∇u|^{n-2} A_u(∇u, ∇u) and the H-system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = H(u) J_u, the paper notes that the spaces of weak solutions remain closed under weak W^{1,n} limits even for approximate problems with a small perturbation in (W^{1,n})*. Can those closure results be exploited to construct counterexamples to regularity as weak limits of singular solutions to perturbed versions of these equations?

evidence.quote: On the other hand, C. Wang [74], see also [40], and the second named author with A. Zatorska-Goldstein [66] have proved that for (2.4) and (2.5) - and for the corresponding approximate problems with a small perturbation in (W1,n)* added to the right hand side - the spaces of weak solutions are closed in the weak topology of W1,n.
We do not know whether these results could be used to construct counterexamples from sequences of singular solutions to perturbed versions of (2.4) and (2.5).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$, let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded smooth domain, and let $N \subset \mathbb{R}^k$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold without boundary, isometrically embedded in $\mathbb{R}^k$. For maps $u \in W^{1,n}(\Omega, N)$ consider the $n$-harmonic map system
$$-\operatorname{div}(|
abla u|^{n-2} 
abla u) = |
abla u|^{n-2}\, A_u(
abla u, 
abla u), \qquad (\star)$$
where $A_u(\cdot,\cdot)$ denotes the second fundamental form of $N$ at $u$, and (for $n=2$, $k=3$) the prescribed mean curvature $H$-system
$$-\operatorname{div}(|
abla u|^{n-2}
abla u) = H(u)\, J_u, \qquad (\star\star)$$
where $H : \mathbb{R}^3 	o \mathbb{R}$ is a bounded smooth function and $J_u = u_{x_1} \wedge u_{x_2}$.

It is known that the set of weak solutions in $W^{1,n}$ to $(\star)$ (respectively $(\star\star)$) is closed under weak $W^{1,n}$ convergence, and more generally, the same closure property holds for the perturbed equations
$$-\operatorname{div}(|
abla u|^{n-2}
abla u) = |
abla u|^{n-2} A_u(
abla u, 
abla u) + f, \qquad -\operatorname{div}(|
abla u|^{n-2}
abla u) = H(u) J_u + f,$$
where $f$ ranges over a small ball in the dual space $(W^{1,n})^*$.

Problem. Determine whether these weak-closure properties can be used to produce counterexamples to regularity for $(\star)$ or $(\star\star)$. More precisely: does there exist a sequence $\{u_j\} \subset W^{1,n}(\Omega, N)$ of weak solutions to perturbed equations of the above form, with perturbations $f_j 	o 0$ in $(W^{1,n})^*$, such that each $u_j$ has a singularity and the weak $W^{1,n}$ limit $u = \lim_j u_j$ is a weak solution of the unperturbed equation $(\star)$ (or $(\star\star)$) which fails to be continuous (or otherwise fails to satisfy known partial regularity)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem ("we do not know whether..."). No published resolution was located that exhibits such counterexamples to regularity for $n$-harmonic maps or $H$-systems via weak limits of singular solutions to perturbed equations. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:1606.07891
status_evidence.snippet: The authors explicitly state they do not know whether the closure results can be used to construct counterexamples from sequences of singular solutions to perturbed versions of the equations.
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an unresolved problem.
